«Какие решения VPN обычно используются на предприятии?» makes the MPLS distractors true: enterprises commonly buy Layer 2 and Layer 3 MPLS VPNs (RFC 4364 §1: «The client may be an enterprise»); the stem must say «которыми управляет само предприятие». Six options for three keys; fourth recall item (the figure 8.1.4 lists); the shared comment does not say MPLS and Frame Relay are provider-managed.
Lecture-level: section «Виртуальные частные сети» (8.1.1: why a VPN is virtual and private, and that a GRE tunnel carries no encryption) has no question.

The one allowed recall item (8.2.1: a clientless VPN is SSL through the browser); key true. «протокол IPsec» is a protocol, not a connection type, so the stem's «тип VPN-соединения» eliminates it. The shared comment explains only the key, not that a client-based VPN needs installed software or that site-to-site tunnels end on gateways.

Distractor «использует двустороннюю аутентификацию с общими ключами или цифровыми сертификатами» is true of SSL VPN: the 8.2.2 table gives SSL «одностороннюю или двустороннюю аутентификацию», and TLS supports client certificates and PSK (RFC 8446 §4.3.2, §2.2). The key «требуется только веб-браузер на узле», copied from the table, holds only for clientless SSL VPN (8.2.1: client software may encrypt with SSL). Second recall item; the comment skips «только определенные устройства».

Third recall item (8.2.4: «несущий протокол – GRE»). «К какому типу протоколов относится GRE?» names no frame: an expert would answer «протокол туннелирования»; ask for GRE's role in GRE over IPsec. The shared comment does not say what the passenger and transport protocols are.

Fourth recall item (8.2.5: DMVPN scales to many VPNs). «Site-to-site VPN» includes DMVPN (figure 8.1.4 lists DMVPN under Site-to-Site VPN), so it is not wrong as worded; 8.2.5 contrasts DMVPN with statically configured site-to-site IPsec and GRE over IPsec. Shared comment restates the key.

Fifth recall item; the stem copies «эмуляции сегмента локальной сети Ethernet с множественным доступом» (8.2.7). The key «MPLS VPN» is too broad: only a Layer 2 MPLS VPN (VPLS, RFC 4762) emulates a LAN segment, a Layer 3 MPLS VPN (RFC 4364) routes. Shared comment.
Lecture-level: sections «Site-to-Site IPSec VPN» (8.2.3: the gateway encapsulates and encrypts, hosts send plain TCP/IP) and «Интерфейс виртуальных туннелей IPsec» (8.2.6) have no question.

Distractor «уровень 3» is true: IPsec protects «all protocols that may be carried over IP (including IP itself)» (RFC 4301 §2.1), tunnel-mode ESP covers the whole inner IP header (RFC 4303 §3.1.2), and the lecture's own table has AH and encryption protecting «пакеты уровня 3»; «от 4 до 7 уровня» (8.3.2) is listed for a lecture change. Seven options; recall beyond q08; shared comment. Layer 3 becomes a key, so a new item.

Recall beyond q08; the stem copies the 8.3.2 list («общих ключей (паролей), цифровых сертификатов или RSA»). Five options; the shared comment restates the key and does not say what the other four functions do.

A «Верно ли утверждение…» true/false item, which rule 6 bars from scored lectures; recall of «без обновления существующих стандартов» (8.3.2). «платформа IPsec» is not the lecture's word («структура», «фреймворк»).
Recall of the framework figure (AH, ESP); seven options for two keys; «использование RSA» differs in form from the bare names; the shared comment does not say which function each distractor serves.

Keys «3DES» and «SEAL» are doubtful against the primary source: RFC 8221 §5 makes ENCR_3DES SHOULD NOT (the lecture says so too), and SEAL is no IETF ESP transform (absent from RFC 8221 and the IANA IPsec encryption registry; one vendor's option). Seven options; recall of figure 8.3.2-1; shared comment. Base the rework on AES (RFC 8221 §5: MUST).

Key «MD5»: HMAC-MD5-96 is MUST NOT for ESP and AH (RFC 8221 §6), and the lecture's own note recommends at least SHA-256 (8.3.5); the 8.3.5 MD5 bullet is listed for a lecture change. Seven options; recall; shared comment.

«функции аутентификации» does not say peer authentication: AH provides data origin authentication (RFC 4302 §1; 8.3.3 «обеспечивает аутентификацию и целостность данных») and 03.10 teaches HMAC as source authentication, so «AH» and «SHA» are defensible. Seven options; recall; shared comment.

The one allowed recall item; key true (group 1 MUST NOT, 2 and 5 SHOULD NOT, RFC 8247 §2.4). The distractor «группы DH 19, 20, 21 и 24» includes group 24, a 2048-bit MODP group, not ECC (RFC 5114 §2.3), which RFC 8247 §2.4 also demotes to SHOULD NOT: drop 24 from it (new answerId; the 8.3.7 sentences on group 24 are listed for a lecture change). «больше не рекомендуется» needs **НЕ** in bold capitals or a positive «устарели»; the comment should say 14–16 and 19–21 remain in use.

Distractor «выполняет аутентификацию узлов IPsec» is defensible: with a pre-shared key the IKE AUTH value is computed with the negotiated prf, usually HMAC (RFC 7296 §2.15), and 03.10 teaches HMAC as source authentication. Replace it (new answerId; q01 stays). The shared comment explains only the key and misnames HMAC «Hashed» (RFC 2104, 8.3.5: Hash-based).
Key true (AES, 8.3.4). Five options; drop one (MD5 or SHA, which are wrong for the same reason). The combined comment explains every option.

Key «MD5»: HMAC-MD5-96 is MUST NOT for AH and ESP (RFC 8221 §6), yet the stem says «используются». «алгоритмы хеширования» leaves only MD5 and SHA among AES, DH and RSA, so the category gives both keys away; five options; shared comment. Rework, e.g. which hash is recommended today (SHA-256, the 8.3.5 note).

«интересный трафик» and «политика IPsec» appear nowhere in the module or earlier in the course. PSK is not an algorithm, so the stem's «алгоритмы … шифрования и хеширования» eliminates it; five options; the shared comment explains only the keys.
Key true (GRE, RFC 2784; 8.1.1). The combined comment explains every option. Passes.
Keys true (8.2.3: a router or a firewall). Five options; «коммутатор DSL» names no device of the course (07.05 has the DSLAM), so drop it. Per-option comments pass.
Key true (8.2.1). The stem's «удаленного доступа» eliminates both site-to-site options, leaving only the two SSL options. The shared comment explains the key only.

Key true. The combined comment is wrong twice: authentication does not «предоставляет … права доступа» (that is authorisation; IPsec authentication verifies the peer by PSK or RSA signature, 8.3.6, RFC 7296 §2.15), and DH lets peers derive a shared secret over an insecure channel (8.3.7), not «сохранять конфиденциальность своих закрытых ключей, совместно используя открытый ключ».

Keys true by figure 8.1.4. The stem asks for «технологии», but the keys are deployment types (site-to-site, remote access) and the distractors technologies (Frame Relay, MPLS). Five options; the combined comment passes.

Distractor «IPSec Virtual Tunnel Interface (VTI) VPN» is defensible from 8.2.6 («упрощает настройку, необходимую для поддержки нескольких сайтов и удаленного доступа»), and dynamic VTIs do terminate remote-access clients; replace it (e.g. with DMVPN; new answerId). Five options; the combined comment, which files VTI under site-to-site only, needs the same change.
Key true (8.1.3, 8.2.3). The shared comment explains why hosts need no client software but not why the client–server architecture and a VPN server at the edge, both remote-access traits, are wrong.

Key true by convention, but «обмениваться общими ключами» suggests the key itself is sent; DH lets each peer compute the same secret from exchanged public values (8.3.7), so reword the key. «инфраструктуре IPsec»: the lecture says «структура». The shared comment explains the key only.

«Какое утверждение характеризует важные свойства…» is unfocused. Key «должен быть статически настроен» fails for DMVPN, a site-to-site VPN (figure 8.1.4) whose spokes build tunnels from what the hub tells them (8.2.5), which also makes «может динамически изменять информацию о соединении» defensible; reword the key to «VPN-шлюзы заранее знают конфигурацию VPN» (8.1.3) and drop that option (five options). Shared comment.

Key true (8.2.3–8.2.4: the original packet is encapsulated in GRE and IPsec headers). The shared comment explains tunnelling but not why disguising packets, one physical medium or a dedicated channel is wrong.
Key true (8.1.1). It is the only option that spells out «виртуальные … частных сетей», the expansion of the stem's «VPN». The shared comment does not address the open-source virtualisation option.

Distractor DMVPN is true: DMVPN runs mGRE over IPsec (8.2.5), so it has the same passenger, carrier (GRE) and transport protocols. Replace it (e.g. SSL VPN; new answerId). No wrong option has a comment.

DMVPN (an mGRE tunnel interface, 8.2.5) and GRE over IPsec also apply their configuration to a virtual tunnel interface, so the stem does not single out VTI. Ask for VTI's own property (IPsec on the virtual interface carries multicast without GRE, 8.2.6). No wrong option has a comment.
Key true (8.2.2). «с помощью функции TLS»: TLS is a protocol (the newer SSL), not a function. No wrong option has a comment.
Key true (8.2.7; RFC 4364 for Layer 3, RFC 4762 VPLS for Layer 2). No wrong option has a comment.

Two distractors are defensible: VTI carries encrypted multicast (8.2.6) and DMVPN is mGRE over IPsec (8.2.5), so both pass routing-protocol multicast across a secure site-to-site VPN. Replace them with options that cannot (e.g. a site-to-site IPsec VPN without GRE, 8.2.4; new answerIds). No wrong option has a comment.

The distinction is false: IPsec authenticates peers with RSA signatures and digital certificates too (8.2.2 table, 8.3.6; RFC 7296 §2.15, §3.6), so GRE over IPsec, DMVPN and VTI all use a PKI. Rework on a property only SSL VPN has (e.g. support limited to web applications and file sharing, 8.2.2). No wrong option has a comment.
Distractor DMVPN is true: its mGRE tunnels, which carry no encryption, are protected by IPsec (8.2.5). Replace it (new answerId). No wrong option has a comment.

Same tested point as q17, and the stem translates the key's name («интерфейсы виртуального туннеля» = Virtual Tunnel Interface). DMVPN and GRE over IPsec also route packets through a virtual tunnel interface for encryption (8.2.5). Rework on another fact (e.g. VTI between sites or hub-and-spoke, 8.2.6); no wrong option has a comment.

«Какие утверждения описывают…» is unfocused. Distractor «для нее требуется, чтобы узлы отправляли трафик TCP/IP через шлюз VPN» is true of a remote-access client too, whose traffic goes to the VPN gateway (figure 8.1.3-2); say «незашифрованный трафик, не зная о VPN» (8.2.3) or replace it. Five options; the shared comment does not say the other two distractors are site-to-site traits.
Key true (3DES is a confidentiality option, 8.3.4). Five options; the shared comment explains the key only and calls the algorithms «протоколами».
Key true (8.2.1: a client-based remote-access VPN needs installed software). Per-option comments pass.
Key true (8.1.1). «масштабируемость» is a VPN benefit, not a method, so the stem's category eliminates it. Shared comment restates the key.

The lecture names the topologies «звезда» and «луч-луч» (8.2.5), not «концентратор-луч»; «узел-узел» and «клиент-узел» render «site» with «узел», which the glossary reserves for host. «site-to-site» is not wrong for DMVPN, whose tunnels all join sites (figure 8.1.4 lists it under Site-to-Site VPN): drop it (five options). Shared comment.

Distractor «чтобы увеличить пропускную способность сети» is defensible from 8.1.2 (VPNs «повышают пропускную способность удаленных подключений»); replace it. The key «поставщикам» clashes with the module's «поставщик услуг» for the provider; 8.2.1 says «подрядчикам и партнерам». Five options; the shared comment skips the bandwidth and connection-check options.

Key true (GRE carries no encryption, 8.1.1). «безопасно передают открытый текст» joins two claims, so the learner cannot tell which one is judged; ask «Шифруют ли все VPN передаваемые данные?» and name GRE in the comment.

Distractor «Site-to-site VPN» is defensible: 8.1.1 and figure 8.1.1 show a home-office router with a site-to-site VPN to the main site. Name a mobile employee with a laptop in the stem. The shared comment does not explain the site-to-site option.
Key true (8.1.4; RFC 4364). The combined comment explains every option; same distinction as q09, from the provider side. Passes.
Key true (AH, RFC 4302; 8.3.3). «IP протокол 50» is not taught in the module and is ESP (RFC 4303 §2), so two options are one distractor; replace it (e.g. GRE). The combined comment passes.

Key true. The comment is false that HMAC ensures data «не перехватываются»: it detects modification and does not stop interception (RFC 2104 §1). «вычисленного хеш-значения» picks the only hash-based option, and RSA signatures also sign a computed hash (8.3.6), so restrict the stem to each packet of an IPsec tunnel. Same tested point as q01.
Key true (8.3.4). «длина ключа не зависит от алгоритма шифрования» does not answer the stem (deterring an attacker), so it is no learner mistake; replace it. The combined comment passes.

«межузловые» renders «site» with «узел», which the glossary reserves for host, and makes the key the longest option (43 characters against 7–13). «публичная» and «частная» are not VPN types, as the comment itself says. The combined comment explains every option.
Keys true (figure 8.1.4). Six options for three keys; no wrong option has a comment.

A scenario; key true. No wrong option has a comment; the firewall option needs one, since 8.1.1 says the firewall provides VPN access for mobile users: it can terminate the VPN, but filtering does not encrypt.

Every distractor is true: «бесклиентное VPN-соединение защищено с помощью SSL…» copies 8.2.1, «site-to-site VPN обычно создается и защищается с использованием … IPsec» copies 8.2.3, and the gateway does encrypt the traffic it sends to a client (one SA per direction, RFC 4301 §4.1). «Какое утверждение является точным описанием…» is unfocused, and the key's point is tested by q36. Propose drop (kb decides); if kept, replace all three distractors.

The one allowed recall item (the 9.1.3 table: propagation delay is the time a frame takes over the path, set by distance and medium); key true, serialization and coding delay are the named confusions of the objective, and the combined comment explains every option. Passes.

Second recall item (9.1.2 «память устройства заполняется и пакеты отбрасываются»); key true (tail drop of the arriving packet). «Джиттер» is also a congestion effect (9.1.3), so the stem should tie the outcome to the arriving packet. The shared comment restates the key; it does not say jitter is the variation of queuing delay and coding delay a fixed source-side time. Rework as a case, e.g. an aggregation or speed-mismatch point whose output queue is full when a packet arrives.

Third recall item (serialization delay, 9.1.3 table); key true. «фиксированное» in the stem eliminates «Джиттер», which is a variation, not a fixed time. The shared comment restates the key. Rework as a case, e.g. the time to put a 1500-byte frame on a 1 Mbit/s link.

«Потеря пакетов» is also caused by varying delay: 9.1.4 says packets that jitter pushes outside the playout buffer are dropped. Jitter is the variation itself («разница в задержке», 9.1.3), not its result. Fourth recall item; the shared comment restates the key. Rework as a playout-buffer case (packets arriving 20, 45, 15 ms apart), which also tests 9.1.4.

The stem copies 9.2.2 «могут занять всю полосу пропускания канала связи». «Видео» is defensible too: the 9.2.4 table calls video «Ресурсоемкость» (greedy) with up to «более чем 20 Мбит/с», enough to fill a slow link. Second recall item; the shared comment explains only FTP. Rework as a case (a file download vs a call and a conference on one uplink), keeping 9.2.2 and 9.2.5 covered.
Recall of «не менее 384 Кбит/с» (9.2.4); key true. The shared comment restates the key and does not say voice needs 30–128 kbit/s and data has no fixed minimum.

«Данные» is also defensible: 9.2.2 gives data «непредсказуемой пропускной способностью» and 9.2.5 says data traffic «может быть постоянным или пульсирующим» (table: «Равномерность/неравномерность»). «неоднородным» is not the lecture's word («нестабильный»). Recall item; shared comment. Rework on video's own trait (packet size and count change every 33 ms).

«Данные» is also defensible for «может быть предсказуемым и равномерным»: 9.2.5 «Трафик управления сетью обычно постоянный и предсказуемый», table «Равномерность/неравномерность». Recall item; the shared comment restates the key.
The one allowed recall item (200 bytes every 20 ms, 9.2.4; UDP without retransmission, 9.2.5); key true (RTP voice over UDP), and each wrong option has its own comment with the right fact. Passes.

«более высокий приоритет UDP» does not say higher than what, and both tables list «Приоритет UDP»; 9.2.4 also says video ports «необходимо присвоить более высокий приоритет», so «Видео» is defensible. Recall item; the shared comment restates the key. Rework as a case on which flow goes ahead of which.

Recall of 9.3.4 (WFQ schedules interactive traffic first). «LLQ» is defensible too: its strict priority queue sends interactive voice ahead of everything (9.3.6), and 9.3.4 itself names voice among WFQ's interactive flows. The shared comment restates the key. Rework on WFQ's own trait (automatic per-flow classification, no user classes).

Two keys are defensible: LLQ is CBWFQ plus a strict priority queue (9.3.6 «Функция LLQ добавляет к CBWFQ строгую очередь по приоритетам»), so LLQ also supports user-defined classes. Recall item; the shared comment restates the key.

The one allowed recall item (9.3.3: FIFO suits large links with little congestion); key true. The stem nearly copies the sentence and says «загруженностью» where the lecture and the glossary say «перегрузка». The shared comment does not say what WFQ, CBWFQ and LLQ add (flows, classes, a priority queue) that only matters under congestion.
Copies 9.3.4 «классифицирует трафик, разделяя его на различные потоки с учетом адресации заголовков пакетов»; third WFQ item of six. Shared comment restates the key.

Copies 9.3.6 «PQ позволяет отправлять чувствительные к задержке данные, например голос, перед пакетами в других очередях»; key true. The shared comment does not say CBWFQ has no strict priority queue. Rework as a case (an administrator needs voice always sent first).

The stem states a wrong mechanism: WFQ classifies flows by header fields (9.3.4) and then weights them; weights do not identify or classify traffic. «CBWFQ» fits «применяет ... веса» too (9.3.5: a class gets «полосу пропускания, вес»). Fourth WFQ item; the shared comment restates the stem.

Lecture-level: «Общие сведения об организации очереди» (9.3.2: queuing is a congestion-management tool that acts only when the link is congested) has no question; the section only supplies the option names.

Recall of the 9.4.4 table «Контроль доступа для каждого запроса»; key true (RFC 1633 §2: admission control per request). Same point as q04. The shared comment restates the key and does not say best effort and DiffServ admit traffic without a request.
Negative stem («не требует»): rewrite positively. Recall of the 9.4.3 table («Никакие специальные механизмы QoS не требуются»); the shared comment restates the key.
The one allowed recall item (DiffServ: classes without signalling, 9.4.5); key true (RFC 2475), each option has its own comment. Passes.

Recall of «Явное сквозное управление доступом к ресурсам» (9.4.4 table), the same point as q01; shared comment. Rework as a case (an application that announces its traffic profile and waits for RSVP reservations).
Recall of «Самая масштабируемая модель» (9.4.3 table); key true and the combined comment explains every option. Rework as a case (an ISP core with millions of flows and no QoS configuration).

The one allowed recall item (9.5.12: excess over the maximum rate is dropped); key true. The shared comment restates the key; it does not say shaping queues the excess instead of dropping it, classification only assigns a class, or that policing may also re-mark.
Recall of 9.5.4; key true. The distractor «Маркировка.» alone ends with a period. The shared comment does not say marking writes the decision into a header field and shaping delays traffic.

The stem copies 9.5.4 «Маркировка означает добавление некоторого значения в заголовок пакета». «802.1Q» is arguably right too: its tag inserts the 3-bit PCP (CoS) value into the frame header (9.5.5; IEEE 802.1Q clause 9.6); only «пакета» vs «кадра» separates them. Recall item; shared comment.

Recall of 9.5.11 (WRED drops TCP early, before the buffer overflows); key true (RFC 7567 AQM). «802.1Q» is a tagging standard, not a buffer tool, so nobody picks it. The shared comment does not say policing has no queue.
The stem copies 9.5.12 «сохраняет лишние пакеты в очереди, а затем планирует их последующую передачу через определенные промежутки времени»; recall item; shared comment repeats the stem.

Lecture-level: «Маркировка на уровне коммутации» (9.5.5: 802.1p CoS, 3 bits, 0–7), «Маркировка на сетевом уровне» (9.5.6), «Поле «Тип обслуживания / Класс трафика»» (9.5.7: DSCP 6 bits, ECN 2), «Значения DSCP» (9.5.8: BE 0, EF 46, AFxy), «Средство выбора класса (CS)» (9.5.9), «Границы доверия» (9.5.10) and «Руководящие принципы политики QoS» (9.5.13) have no question.

Key true (9.5.4: L3 marking is carried end to end; DSCP survives routed hops, CoS does not). The shared comment lists the L2/L3 facts but does not say 802.1Q carries the L2 CoS, not an L3 marking, and opens with a filler sentence.

Key true: the boundary is where QoS markings start to be trusted. The lecture prose says only that marking near the source «определяет границу доверия» (figure 9.5.10 shades the trusted part). The shared comment does not say the boundary blocks no traffic (untrusted traffic enters and is re-marked) and that re-marking happens at it.

Five options for two keys. Without «для важных приложений» (9.5.2) the key «удаление пакетов с низким приоритетом» is itself packet loss, which the stem asks to prevent. The shared comment lists the three approaches but not why banning bursts, a smaller buffer or disabling queuing is wrong.

Scenario; key true. The stem asks for «причину этой проблемы» while naming congestion as the cause, and 9.1.3 lists «некорректной организации очереди» among the causes of varying delay, so «организация очереди» can be argued; ask for the name of the variation. The shared comment does not say buffering is the remedy (playout buffer) and latency the delay itself.
Key true (9.3.3). The shared comment explains FIFO only; it does not say WFQ queues per flow, CBWFQ per class and LLQ adds a strict priority queue.
Scenario; key true (LLQ = CBWFQ + strict priority queue). The shared comment does not say CBWFQ has no strict priority queue, WFQ classifies flows automatically and FIFO has one queue.
Five options for two keys; the distractors are IntServ (connection-oriented, signalling) and DiffServ (priority) traits, good mistakes. The shared comment does not name the model each one describes.

Five options for two keys. «удаленные пакеты» also reads as "remote packets"; the lecture says «отбрасываются» / «потерянные». Keys true (RTP voice over UDP is not retransmitted; ITU-T G.114 150 ms one-way). The comment does not say 384 kbit/s and unpredictability belong to video. Same stem as q30.

Negative stem («нельзя»). «ICMP» is also right: it has no congestion control, so WRED drops do not slow it (RFC 7567 §4: unresponsive flows «do not slow down when congestion occurs»); replace it with TCP-carried traffic (e.g. HTTP; new answerId, item keeps q09). WRED still drops UDP; it only cannot make UDP back off. The comment restates the key.
